scope: 2024正式AAAI研究正文：第38卷1—19期所有技术论文及第20期AI for Social Impact和Senior Member完整论文；不以首次在线日期、会前录用数或全套联办总数替代。
scope_outside_caveat: 第21期含IAAI 44条及EAAI 37条（含1条作业摘要），它们属于独立联办会议/教育研讨会，单列保留书目，未伪称已作其AI4S精筛；AAAI学生/博士/本科摘要及Demo按本批正文范围不计。没有把这些条目宣称为非AI4S。
match_method: 2439条原记录的稳定官网文章ID、归一题名及作者顺序逐条双向匹配；88条新增再与准确DOI的出版方Crossref登记核对完整题名、作者、卷期页码。不是只比较总数。

new_review_records.title: HarvestNet: A Dataset for Detecting Smallholder Farming Activity Using Harvest Piles and Remote Sensing
new_review_records.rationale: 利用卫星收获堆数据与深度视觉基线识别埃塞俄比亚小农耕地，使用地面标签验证并量化既有地图漏检面积，直接贡献农业遥感监测。

new_review_records.title: Harnessing Network Effect for Fake News Mitigation: Selecting Debunkers via Self-Imitation Learning
new_review_records.rationale: 自模仿强化学习选择社交网络辟谣节点，主要优化平台信息传播干预的算法表现，未报告实证社会机制发现或实际社会干预效果。

new_review_records.title: Spatial-Logic-Aware Weakly Supervised Learning for Flood Mapping on Earth Imagery
new_review_records.rationale: 将空间逻辑推理与弱监督神经网络训练结合，从粗噪标签推断高分辨率洪水范围，真实洪水数据验证直接支持灾害地学制图。

new_review_records.title: Unveiling the Tapestry of Automated Essay Scoring: A Comprehensive Investigation of Accuracy, Fairness, and Generalizability
new_review_records.rationale: 研究作文自动评分模型的精度、公平性和跨提示泛化，评价对象是模型基准表现，未研究实际学习、认知或教育干预机制。

new_review_records.title: Graph Bayesian Optimization for Multiplex Influence Maximization
new_review_records.rationale: 图贝叶斯优化解决多信息影响最大化，商品传播是主要动机，实验为通用社交图算法比较，未提供独立科学对象研究。

new_review_records.title: Fairness-Aware Structured Pruning in Transformers
new_review_records.rationale: 通过裁剪Transformer注意力头降低社会偏见并控制语言建模损失，是通用模型压缩及公平性研究，未见科学或工程对象。

new_review_records.title: Estimating On-Road Transportation Carbon Emissions from Open Data of Road Network and Origin-Destination Flow Data
new_review_records.rationale: 将道路网络、区域和出行OD构成分层异质图，利用真实数据预测道路交通碳排放，AI直接提供环境排放估计方法。

new_review_records.title: Towards Automatic Boundary Detection for Human-AI Collaborative Hybrid Essay in Education
new_review_records.rationale: 检测人机混写作文的生成内容边界，主要是文本来源鉴别及模型性能实验，未见独立教育科学或认知研究贡献。

new_review_records.title: Pre-trained Online Contrastive Learning for Insurance Fraud Detection
new_review_records.rationale: 在线对比学习识别医疗保险欺诈，是常规保险风控业务，不因含医疗术语而成为生命科学研究。

new_review_records.title: UV-SAM: Adapting Segment Anything Model for Urban Village Identification
new_review_records.rationale: 将SAM适配城中村遥感边界分割，并用多年识别结果分析数量与面积趋势，AI直接为城市土地与居住环境变化研究提供测量工具。

new_review_records.title: Causally Aware Generative Adversarial Networks for Light Pollution Control
new_review_records.rationale: 对七座城市住宅区光污染的建筑类型驱动因素作因果分析，并将发现引导GAN生成污染图，直接研究光污染成因与照明布局。

new_review_records.title: Multiple-Source Localization from a Single-Snapshot Observation Using Graph Bayesian Optimization
new_review_records.rationale: BOSouL以图贝叶斯优化求扩散源，实验验证通用图结构和扩散模型上的定位性能，危害传播只是动机，摘要未给出具体疾病、物理或社会科学研究任务。

new_review_records.title: Leveraging Opposite Gender Interaction Ratio as a Path towards Fairness in Online Dating Recommendations Based on User Sexual Orientation
new_review_records.rationale: 通过重加权及重排序改善在线约会推荐的群体公平性，主要是平台推荐服务算法，未显示独立行为或社会机制研究。

new_review_records.title: AI-Based Energy Transportation Safety: Pipeline Radial Threat Estimation Using Intelligent Sensing System
new_review_records.rationale: 融合分布式光纤声学信号的多视角多域特征，并用预训练迁移辨识外部事件的径向位置与威胁，在真实场景验证管道物理安全感知。

new_review_records.title: TAU: Trajectory Data Augmentation with Uncertainty for Next POI Recommendation
new_review_records.rationale: 补全轨迹伪标签并校准不确定性以提高下一个兴趣点推荐精度，主要为推荐业务与通用增强机制，未研究明确科学对象。

new_review_records.title: Recommender Ecosystems: A Mechanism Design Perspective on Holistic Modeling and Optimization
new_review_records.rationale: 机制设计视角讨论推荐生态长期效用与激励，属推荐系统方法展望，未展示AI实质参与独立科学任务；不是因Senior Member栏目自动排除。

new_review_records.title: Model Reprogramming: Resource-Efficient Cross-Domain Machine Learning
new_review_records.rationale: 正式8页实质方法综述，第2.2节及表2具体比较模型重编程用于自闭症脑相关图、生化序列毒性和抗菌肽预测，以及蛋白序列生成；科学贡献由这些已实现用例支撑，不仅是通用资源效率愿景。

new_review_records.title: Conversational Modeling for Constraint Satisfaction
new_review_records.rationale: 主张以对话自动化约束建模并讨论未来方向，工厂调度只是举例，未给出AI参与确定物理科学研究的实际方法或实证。

new_review_records.title: Integrated Systems for Computational Scientific Discovery
new_review_records.rationale: 正文综合科学发现组件与已有集成系统，具体讨论DENDRAL/Meta-DENDRAL化学结构和碎裂规律、Bacon物理定律及Fahrenheit电化学实验，属于具有已实现科学方法证据的实质综述；未来完整自主系统不当作已完成实验。

new_review_records.title: Towards a More Burkean Approach to Computational Social Choice
new_review_records.rationale: 讨论计算社会选择应更多考虑既有政治决策机制，是研究方向及规范性立场文章，未显示AI工具用于明确社会科学问题的具体研究。

new_review_records.title: Regeneration Learning: A Learning Paradigm for Data Generation
new_review_records.rationale: 再生学习为文本、语音、音乐、图像等通用生成任务提出框架，没有具体科学或物理工程研究对象。

new_review_records.title: The Fairness Fair: Bringing Human Perception into Collective Decision-Making
new_review_records.rationale: 讨论公平分配应考虑人的公平感知并提出跨学科挑战，主要为方向性论述，摘要未显示AI方法产生具体行为研究结果。

new_review_records.title: Temporal Fairness in Multiwinner Voting
new_review_records.rationale: 统一多轮多赢家投票的时间公平框架，核心是一般机制与算法分析，未显示AI作为工具实质参与明确社会科学对象的研究。

new_review_records.rationale: 综述混合物品和负担的公平分配算法与开放问题，主要是通用博弈与分配理论，未提供AI用于确定科学研究任务的证据；不因综述类型一律排除。

new_review_records.rationale: 综述视觉语言Transformer的偏见、鲁棒性及可解释性，属于通用可信AI方法梳理，未显示具体科学对象上的实质贡献。

The Thirty-Eighth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence was held on February 20–27, 2024 in VANCOUVER, CANADA. The program chairs were Jennifer Dy (Northeastern University, USA) and Sriraam Natarajan (University of Texas at Dallas, USA).

AAAI-24 welcomed submissions on research that advances artificial intelligence, broadly conceived. The conference featured technical paper presentations, special tracks, invited speakers, workshops, tutorials, poster sessions, senior member presentations, competitions, and exhibit programs. Many of these activities were tailored to the theme of bridges and were selected according to the highest standards, with additional programs for students and young researchers. The purpose of this year’s Bridge Program was to tap into new sources of innovation by cultivating collaboration between two or more communities directed towards a common goal including distinct subfields of AI, such as planning and learning, or different disciplines that contribute to and benefit from AI, such as AI and the humanities.

The conference scope included machine learning (deep learning, statistical learning, etc), natural language processing, computer vision, data mining, multiagent systems, knowledge representation, human-in-the-loop AI, search, planning, reasoning, robotics and perception, and ethics. In addition to fundamental work that focused on any one of these areas, AAAI-24 encouraged work across technical areas of AI, (e.g., machine learning and computer vision; computer vision and natural language processing; or machine learning and planning), bridges between AI and a related research area (e.g., neuroscience; cognitive science) or developing AI techniques in the context of important application domains, such as healthcare, sustainability, transportation, and commerce.

The conference also continued its tradition of colocating with the long-running Innovative Applications of Artificial Intelligence conference (IAAI-24). IAAI-24 was cochaired by Alex Wong (University of Waterloo, Canada), YuHao Chen (University of Waterloo, Canada) and Jan R. Seyler (Festo, Germany). The IAAI-24 papers are included in this proceedings. Also included are the papers from the Symposium on Educational Advances in Artificial Intelligence (EAAI-24). EAAI-24 was cochaired by Marion Neumann (Washington University, USA) and Stephanie Rosenthal (Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, USA)
The proceedings have been published in 21 consecutive issues. This issue (volume 38 no. 16) consists of 1207 pages and 2 tracks:

AAAI Technical Track on Multiagent Systems

The Thirty-Eighth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence was held on February 20–27, 2024 in VANCOUVER, CANADA. The program chairs were Jennifer Dy (Northeastern University, USA) and Sriraam Natarajan (University of Texas at Dallas, USA).

AAAI-24 welcomed submissions on research that advances artificial intelligence, broadly conceived. The conference featured technical paper presentations, special tracks, invited speakers, workshops, tutorials, poster sessions, senior member presentations, competitions, and exhibit programs. Many of these activities were tailored to the theme of bridges and were selected according to the highest standards, with additional programs for students and young researchers. The purpose of this year’s Bridge Program was to tap into new sources of innovation by cultivating collaboration between two or more communities directed towards a common goal including distinct subfields of AI, such as planning and learning, or different disciplines that contribute to and benefit from AI, such as AI and the humanities.

The conference scope included machine learning (deep learning, statistical learning, etc), natural language processing, computer vision, data mining, multiagent systems, knowledge representation, human-in-the-loop AI, search, planning, reasoning, robotics and perception, and ethics. In addition to fundamental work that focused on any one of these areas, AAAI-24 encouraged work across technical areas of AI, (e.g., machine learning and computer vision; computer vision and natural language processing; or machine learning and planning), bridges between AI and a related research area (e.g., neuroscience; cognitive science) or developing AI techniques in the context of important application domains, such as healthcare, sustainability, transportation, and commerce.

The conference also continued its tradition of colocating with the long-running Innovative Applications of Artificial Intelligence conference (IAAI-24). IAAI-24 was cochaired by Alex Wong (University of Waterloo, Canada), YuHao Chen (University of Waterloo, Canada) and Jan R. Seyler (Festo, Germany). The IAAI-24 papers are included in this proceedings. Also included are the papers from the Symposium on Educational Advances in Artificial Intelligence (EAAI-24). EAAI-24 was cochaired by Marion Neumann (Washington University, USA) and Stephanie Rosenthal (Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, USA)
The proceedings have been published in 21 consecutive issues. This issue (volume 38 no. 17) consists of 1304 pages and 1 tracks:

The Thirty-Eighth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence was held on February 20–27, 2024 in VANCOUVER, CANADA. The program chairs were Jennifer Dy (Northeastern University, USA) and Sriraam Natarajan (University of Texas at Dallas, USA).

AAAI-24 welcomed submissions on research that advances artificial intelligence, broadly conceived. The conference featured technical paper presentations, special tracks, invited speakers, workshops, tutorials, poster sessions, senior member presentations, competitions, and exhibit programs. Many of these activities were tailored to the theme of bridges and were selected according to the highest standards, with additional programs for students and young researchers. The purpose of this year’s Bridge Program was to tap into new sources of innovation by cultivating collaboration between two or more communities directed towards a common goal including distinct subfields of AI, such as planning and learning, or different disciplines that contribute to and benefit from AI, such as AI and the humanities.

The conference scope included machine learning (deep learning, statistical learning, etc), natural language processing, computer vision, data mining, multiagent systems, knowledge representation, human-in-the-loop AI, search, planning, reasoning, robotics and perception, and ethics. In addition to fundamental work that focused on any one of these areas, AAAI-24 encouraged work across technical areas of AI, (e.g., machine learning and computer vision; computer vision and natural language processing; or machine learning and planning), bridges between AI and a related research area (e.g., neuroscience; cognitive science) or developing AI techniques in the context of important application domains, such as healthcare, sustainability, transportation, and commerce.

The conference also continued its tradition of colocating with the long-running Innovative Applications of Artificial Intelligence conference (IAAI-24). IAAI-24 was cochaired by Alex Wong (University of Waterloo, Canada), YuHao Chen (University of Waterloo, Canada) and Jan R. Seyler (Festo, Germany). The IAAI-24 papers are included in this proceedings. Also included are the papers from the Symposium on Educational Advances in Artificial Intelligence (EAAI-24). EAAI-24 was cochaired by Marion Neumann (Washington University, USA) and Stephanie Rosenthal (Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, USA)

The Thirty-Eighth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence was held on February 20–27, 2024 in VANCOUVER, CANADA. The program chairs were Jennifer Dy (Northeastern University, USA) and Sriraam Natarajan (University of Texas at Dallas, USA).

AAAI-24 welcomed submissions on research that advances artificial intelligence, broadly conceived. The conference featured technical paper presentations, special tracks, invited speakers, workshops, tutorials, poster sessions, senior member presentations, competitions, and exhibit programs. Many of these activities were tailored to the theme of bridges and were selected according to the highest standards, with additional programs for students and young researchers. The purpose of this year’s Bridge Program was to tap into new sources of innovation by cultivating collaboration between two or more communities directed towards a common goal including distinct subfields of AI, such as planning and learning, or different disciplines that contribute to and benefit from AI, such as AI and the humanities.

The conference scope included machine learning (deep learning, statistical learning, etc), natural language processing, computer vision, data mining, multiagent systems, knowledge representation, human-in-the-loop AI, search, planning, reasoning, robotics and perception, and ethics. In addition to fundamental work that focused on any one of these areas, AAAI-24 encouraged work across technical areas of AI, (e.g., machine learning and computer vision; computer vision and natural language processing; or machine learning and planning), bridges between AI and a related research area (e.g., neuroscience; cognitive science) or developing AI techniques in the context of important application domains, such as healthcare, sustainability, transportation, and commerce.

The conference also continued its tradition of colocating with the long-running Innovative Applications of Artificial Intelligence conference (IAAI-24). IAAI-24 was cochaired by Alex Wong (University of Waterloo, Canada), YuHao Chen (University of Waterloo, Canada) and Jan R. Seyler (Festo, Germany). The IAAI-24 papers are included in this proceedings. Also included are the papers from the Symposium on Educational Advances in Artificial Intelligence (EAAI-24). EAAI-24 was cochaired by Marion Neumann (Washington University, USA) and Stephanie Rosenthal (Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, USA)

The proceedings have been published in 21 consecutive issues. This issue (volume 38 no. 20) consists of 836 pages and 6 tracks:

The Thirty-Eighth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence was held on February 20–27, 2024 in VANCOUVER, CANADA. The program chairs were Jennifer Dy (Northeastern University, USA) and Sriraam Natarajan (University of Texas at Dallas, USA).

AAAI-24 welcomed submissions on research that advances artificial intelligence, broadly conceived. The conference featured technical paper presentations, special tracks, invited speakers, workshops, tutorials, poster sessions, senior member presentations, competitions, and exhibit programs. Many of these activities were tailored to the theme of bridges and were selected according to the highest standards, with additional programs for students and young researchers. The purpose of this year’s Bridge Program was to tap into new sources of innovation by cultivating collaboration between two or more communities directed towards a common goal including distinct subfields of AI, such as planning and learning, or different disciplines that contribute to and benefit from AI, such as AI and the humanities.

The conference scope included machine learning (deep learning, statistical learning, etc), natural language processing, computer vision, data mining, multiagent systems, knowledge representation, human-in-the-loop AI, search, planning, reasoning, robotics and perception, and ethics. In addition to fundamental work that focused on any one of these areas, AAAI-24 encouraged work across technical areas of AI, (e.g., machine learning and computer vision; computer vision and natural language processing; or machine learning and planning), bridges between AI and a related research area (e.g., neuroscience; cognitive science) or developing AI techniques in the context of important application domains, such as healthcare, sustainability, transportation, and commerce.

The conference also continued its tradition of colocating with the long-running Innovative Applications of Artificial Intelligence conference (IAAI-24). IAAI-24 was cochaired by Alex Wong (University of Waterloo, Canada), YuHao Chen (University of Waterloo, Canada) and Jan R. Seyler (Festo, Germany). The IAAI-24 papers are included in this proceedings. Also included are the papers from the Symposium on Educational Advances in Artificial Intelligence (EAAI-24). EAAI-24 was cochaired by Marion Neumann (Washington University, USA) and Stephanie Rosenthal (Carnegie Mellon University, Pittsburgh, USA)
The proceedings have been published in 21 consecutive issues. This issue (volume 38 no. 21) consists of 1146 pages and 14 tracks:
